subtitle: A report of ARPANET host status from June 5 through June 16, 1972.

tldr.problem: Network participants needed regular reports about which hosts were accessible and available as servers.
tldr.mechanism: The report gives host status and daily test results for June 5 through June 16, with notes about testing interruptions and user-only hosts.
tldr.outcome: RFC 362 updates RFC 353 and was later obsoleted by RFC 366; it notes a new MIT Math Lab server and an ARPA Terminal IMP installation.

sections.title: Host Status and Installations
sections.content:
The report covers most Network Hosts from June 5 to June 16. During this period, the MIT Math Lab PDP-10, Network Address 198, became a server. The ARPA Terminal IMP, Network 156, was installed in Arlington, Virginia, on June 16.

No testing was done on June 6 during an attempt to install the new IMP system. No testing was done on June 9 because the prototype Terminal IMP was being used for software debugging.
sections.plainLanguage: The MIT Math Lab PDP-10 became a server, and an ARPA Terminal IMP was installed. Two dates have no test results because of installation work and software debugging.

sections.title: Daily Host Test Results
sections.content:
The daily table records host responses using O for Open, D for Dead, H for Half Open, R for Refused, T for Timed out, and F for Full. Full means a host opened a connection, reported that all Network ports were in use, and immediately closed the connection.

A timed-out host did not complete the ICP and open a connection within 60 seconds. The report also marks sites that said their systems might not be available at those times.
sections.plainLanguage: The codes describe whether each host opened, refused, or failed to complete a connection. A timeout means the host did not open within 60 seconds.

sections.title: Excluded Hosts and Reported Roles
sections.content:
Hosts intended to be users only, including Terminal IMPs and the Network Control Center, were excluded from daily testing. The report also shows a separate table of host roles and predictions, including servers, user-only systems, and systems expected to become servers.

The memo identifies the BBN Terminal IMP as a prototype that was frequently disconnected while its programs were being refined and debugged.
sections.plainLanguage: The report does not test every system daily. It explains that user-only equipment and the prototype BBN Terminal IMP were excluded for different reasons.
